audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant', rule final (final stress), in the dominant set/not in the strict set rests on Salminen 2016, a full JCU PhD reference grammar and the only grammar of sand1278 in Glottolog; I downloaded the open PDF and confirmed the quotation verbatim at sec. 2.2.1 (p.30) and the phonological-word statement at 2.4.4 (p.45). The grammar itself documents the non-strictness (stress-neutral delimitative enclitic =an; recent loans with non-final stress; lexical penults wüxan/ngüñan), so 'dominant, not strict' final stress is exactly right. No instrumental or later prosodic study of this variety exists in Glottolog or on the web (Noyer 1991/2013 and Kim 2008 are San Mateo / San Francisco del Mar, different languoids). Action: no reclassification; fill the empty top-level cite/loc/grade fields from sources[0] with locator 'Salminen 2016 sec. 2.2.1 p.30 (PDF 53); sec. 2.4.4 p.45 (PDF 68)' and register the now-copies we hold.

sources.citation: Salminen 2016, A grammar of Umbeyajts, sec. 2.2.1 and 2.4.4 (full PDF from researchonline.jcu.edu.au/50066)
sources.quote: STRESS. Stress is characterised by high or rising pitch. It is linked to the last syllable of a phonological word (see 2.4.4), which typically consists of a stem and all its affixes. Stress thus shifts as soon as suffixes are added

sources.citation: Salminen, Mikko Benjamin. 2016. A grammar of Umbeyajts as spoken by the Ikojts people of San Dionisio del Mar, Oaxaca, Mexico. PhD thesis, James Cook University. xix+482 pp. https://researchonline.jcu.edu.au/50066/
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Stress is characterised by high or rising pitch. It is linked to the last syllable of a phonological word ... Stress thus shifts as soon as suffixes are added' ([sa'haw], [saha'wan], [taha'was], [tahawa'san]); 2.4.4: phonological word 'receives stress on the final syllables'; the delimitative postclitic =an never shifts stress (mi-kiambáh=an); 2.6.2.1: recent Spanish/Zapotec loans 'may ... have a non-word-final stress pattern'; footnote (the text layer) notes wüxan, ngüñan always penultimate. Supports final stress as dominant-not-exceptionless.

sources.quote: Pan-Huave transcription conventions (Radin's pre-1914 San Dionisio field notes included): 'la sílaba que lleva el acento fonético cuando es regular, o sea la última sílaba' and 'en el caso regular en que es la última sílaba que lleva el acento primario, se suprime el signo' — final stress treated as the regular case across the Huave varieties. Comparative dictionary, not a description of sand1278 stress per se.
sources.locator: front matter p.xiii (PDF p.14) and 'Acento y tono' p.xix (PDF p.19)
sources.note: Only other open work with San Dionisio data and an explicit (pan-Huave) statement that regular primary stress is on the last syllable; corroboration only, does not change the classification. downloaded now.
